---
name: bili-note
description: Extract Bilibili videos and opus/article posts into readable Markdown knowledge notes. Use when the user asks to 提取/提炼/总结/整理 B站 or bilibili video/图文/动态/opus content, save a B站 note to a local knowledge base, include useful comments, handle multi-part videos, fetch B站 AI subtitles, download opus images, or fall back to audio transcription.
---

# Bili Note

Turn Bilibili videos and image-text posts into searchable, reusable Markdown knowledge notes. For videos, fetch subtitles first; if unavailable, transcribe the audio. For image-text posts, extract the main text, images, and code blocks first. When the user requests comments, fetch them and filter out irrelevant discussions.

Network or logged-in operations must use `web-access` first.

Web AI subtitles currently only support the Chrome + `web-access` route: let the logged-in Bilibili page request the subtitle API itself. Do not treat Edge, Playwright ephemeral browsers, or native CDP ports as equivalent alternatives unless the script explicitly supports them.

Bili Note shares reusable local resources with DyNote. The default shared directory is `%USERPROFILE%\.cache\rimagination-notes`, and the default Qwen3-ASR environment is `%USERPROFILE%\.cache\rimagination-notes\qwen3-asr-venv`. If either skill has already installed Qwen3-ASR, the other must reuse it first and avoid duplicate installation. Hugging Face, Whisper, and faster-whisper caches are reused according to the machine's common cache.

## Subtitle Density and Visual Understanding

For Bilibili videos, fetch subtitles first, but subtitles/transcripts do not equal complete understanding. If a long video has noticeably few subtitle characters, the core information may be in visuals, PPT slides, blackboard writing, code demos, screen operations, or un-narrated segments.

- After archiving, you must read `metadata/note_budget.json`. If `visual_dependency.needs_visual_review=true`, do not write sparse subtitles into a complete study note.
- In this case, adopt more suitable techniques first: extract representative keyframes or screenshots, then perform OCR or multimodal visual understanding; re-fetch web AI subtitles or supplement with local automatic speech recognition when necessary.
- If the currently connected model or tool cannot view images, you must tell the user: keyframe understanding is an advanced visual capability requiring multimodal models, OCR tools, or manual review; currently only limited notes based on subtitles/metadata can be generated with coverage noted.
- The final note and user reply should relay `visual_dependency.warnings` and state whether visual evidence has been supplemented.

## Dependencies and Environment Check

The default route aims for zero third-party Python dependencies: video metadata, public subtitles, image-text body, image lists, comments, archiving, evidence indexes, and note budgets are all done with the standard library. Web AI subtitles and audio transcription are enhancement routes, not startup requirements.

On first use, machine change, suspected missing dependencies, or before using web AI subtitles / audio transcription fallback, run first:

```powershell
$skill = "$env:USERPROFILE\.codex\skills\bili-note"
$py = "python"
& $py "$skill\scripts\check_environment.py"
```

Choose the route based on the results:

- `public_subtitles_comments_archive=OK`: prefer the default subtitle/image-text, comment, and archiving flow.
- `browser_ai_subtitles=OK`: when the public API only returns `ai-zh` and `subtitle_url` is empty, use Chrome + `web-access` web AI subtitles.
- `audio_asr_fallback=OK`: only use audio transcription when both subtitles and web AI subtitles are unavailable and the user truly needs a full transcript. Prefer shared Qwen3-ASR for Chinese or unspecified languages; prefer Whisper-family backends for explicitly foreign-language videos.
- When an enhancement capability is missing, only state that route is temporarily unavailable; do not claim the entire skill is unusable.
- Web login state is only used via `web-access` authorized Chrome pages; do not read or copy cookies/profiles, and do not force-kill the user's browser process. Without Chrome + `web-access`, skip web AI subtitles and explain the coverage.

## Default Flow

1. Clarify what the user wants: video or image-text link, whether comments are needed, save path, whether full materials or just distilled content are required.
2. If it's the first use, dependency status is unclear, subtitle fetching failed, or the user requests audio transcription, use `check_environment.py` first to determine available routes.
3. Prefer `run_bili_note.py` to one-click complete automatable parts. It automatically recognizes `/video/BV...`, `/opus/...`, `/dynamic/...`, or plain opus ids.
4. For image-text/posts, use the `extract_bilibili_opus.py` route: fetch body, title, author, publish time, images, code blocks, and image-text evidence index; fetch image-text comments when the user adds `--comments`.
5. For videos, prefer downloading subtitles:
   - When normal subtitle URLs are available, use `--download-subtitles` directly.
   - If the normal API shows `ai-zh` but `subtitle_url` is empty, do not say "no subtitles"; switch to the "web AI subtitles" flow.
   - If subtitles are still unavailable, download audio as needed and transcribe with local automatic speech recognition. Prefer Qwen3-ASR for Chinese, and Whisper-family backends for explicitly foreign languages.
6. When the user requests comments, use `--comments` to fetch top-level and child comments; filter out check-ins, resource requests, ads, chitchat, and other non-technical content when writing the note.
7. Archive raw materials: store complete subtitles or image-text body, images, full comments, metadata, and JSONL indexes in a long-term directory next to the knowledge base.
8. Set targets before writing: you must read `metadata/note_budget.json` first, using the recommended character range, compression ratio target, writing granularity, interaction quality multiplier, evidence block count, and `visual_dependency` as writing goals for this note. Videos are benchmarked by duration, subtitle characters, evidence blocks, comment volume, and interaction quality; image-text posts by body length, images/code/evidence blocks, comment volume, and interaction quality.
   - If `visual_dependency.risk` is `medium` or `high`, supplement keyframes/OCR/multimodal visual understanding first, or clearly tell the user that visual understanding capability is currently lacking and a complete analysis cannot be written.
9. Write Markdown according to budget: default to "learning-oriented notes", aiming for humans or Agents to gain concepts, methods, judgment criteria, practical steps, and self-test questions as if finishing a lesson or tutorial; decide detail level by budget, and do not write long courses and short videos with similar word counts. Place sources, coverage, and archive paths in the latter part. Body evidence defaults to academic-style numbering like `[1][2]`, without directly piling long evidence IDs.
10. Verify after writing: use `score_bili_note.py` to validate note character count, compression ratio, per-minute/per-article density, and evidence citation ratio. Scoring is only for QA and fine-tuning, not a substitute for pre-writing targets; when too short, prioritize adding "learning takeaways, knowledge maps, concept cards, practical workflows, pitfalls, self-test questions" rather than just stacking part summaries or paragraph summaries.

## Common Commands

Set the skill path first in PowerShell:

```powershell
$skill = "$env:USERPROFILE\.codex\skills\bili-note"
$py = "python"
```

### 0. Check Dependencies and Available Routes

```powershell
& $py "$skill\scripts\check_environment.py"
```

Output JSON when other scripts need to read it:

```powershell
& $py "$skill\scripts\check_environment.py" --json
```

### 1. One-Click Extraction and Archiving

Use the main entry point by default. It automatically skips existing outputs, suitable for resumable runs.

```powershell
& $py "$skill\scripts\run_bili_note.py" "https://www.bilibili.com/video/BVxxxx/" `
  --work-dir ".\tmp_bili_extract" `
 --archive-dir "D:\knowledge\知识库\Rag技术\原始材料\BVxxxx_视频短标题" `
  --comments
```

Image-text/posts also use the same entry point:

```powershell
& $py "$skill\scripts\run_bili_note.py" "https://www.bilibili.com/opus/1194341967364882439" `
 --work-dir ".\tmp_bili_opus" `
  --archive-dir "D:\knowledge\知识库\Rag技术\原始材料\O1194341967364882439_图文短标题" `
  --comments
```

If you only want to save the image-text body and image URLs without downloading image files, add:

```powershell
--no-download-images
```

If the normal API has no subtitles but the web player can get AI subtitles, first use `web-access` to open the video page in logged-in Chrome and obtain the target id, then add:

```powershell
--browser-target "CDP_TARGET_ID"
```

After running, check first:

- `bili_note_run_report.md`: what ran this time, what was skipped, where to read next.
- `archive_dir/indexes/证据索引.jsonl`: image-text/subtitle/comment evidence blocks citable when writing summaries.
- `archive_dir/indexes/图文全集.md`: complete image-text body collection.
- `archive_dir/indexes/字幕全集.md`: complete subtitle collection.
- `archive_dir/metadata/note_budget.json`: recommended note characters, compression ratio, writing granularity, and visual dependency hints when subtitles are sparse.

### 2. Fetch Metadata and Part List

```powershell
& $py "$skill\scripts\extract_bilibili.py" "BVxxxx" --out ".\tmp_bili_extract"
```

### 3. Download Normal Public Subtitles

```powershell
& $py "$skill\scripts\extract_bilibili.py" "BVxxxx" --out ".\tmp_bili_extract" --parts all --download-subtitles
```

### 4. Download Web AI Subtitles

When `subtitle_probe.json` contains `ai-zh` but `subtitle_url` is empty, use this route. The current script requires Chrome + `web-access` proxy APIs `/targets` and `/eval`; native Edge/Chrome DevTools ports cannot be passed directly to this script.

1. Use `web-access` to open the Bilibili video page in logged-in Chrome and confirm the page has loaded.
2. Check the browser target id:

```powershell
curl.exe -s http://localhost:3456/targets
```

3. Download AI subtitles:

```powershell
& $py "$skill\scripts\fetch_browser_ai_subtitles.py" --target "CDP_TARGET_ID" --out ".\tmp_bili_extract"
```

Outputs include:

- `browser_ai_subtitle_urls.json`: AI subtitle URL for each part.
- `browser_ai_subtitle_manifest.json`: download manifest.
- `browser_ai_subtitles\*.txt`: plain text subtitles.
- `browser_ai_subtitles\*.srt`: SRT subtitles.
- `browser_ai_subtitles\*.subtitle.json`: Bilibili raw subtitle JSON.

This route lets the Bilibili page request `/x/player/wbi/v2` itself using login state, without reading or printing browser cookies.

If downloaded AI subtitles are obviously garbled or unrelated to the title or course topic, do not treat them as reliable full text. Prioritize marking "AI subtitle quality unusable", then consider ASR fallback; if ASR is also unavailable, only generate a limited study guide based on part titles, descriptions, comments, and metadata, clearly stating limitations.

### 5. Fetch Comments

```powershell
& $py "$skill\scripts\extract_bilibili.py" "BVxxxx" --out ".\tmp_bili_extract" --comments
```

For image-text comments, use the main entry point or the image-text script:

```powershell
& $py "$skill\scripts\extract_bilibili_opus.py" "https://www.bilibili.com/opus/1194341967364882439" --out ".\tmp_bili_opus" --comments
```

After fetching, check `comments.md` and `comments_raw.json`. When writing the final note, only keep comments related to the content topic, corrections, technical supplements, practical experience, and valuable questions.

### 6. Audio Transcription Fallback

Only use local automatic speech recognition when both subtitles and web AI subtitles are unavailable. Do not default to full transcription for long videos unless explicitly requested. For Chinese or unspecified languages, `--asr-backend auto` defaults to preferring shared Qwen3-ASR; for explicitly foreign-language videos, use Whisper-family backends.

```powershell
& $py "$skill\scripts\extract_bilibili.py" "BVxxxx" --out ".\tmp_bili_extract" --parts "1,10,38" --download-audio --transcribe --asr-backend auto --asr-model base
```

Install the shared environment before first use of Qwen3-ASR:

```powershell
& $py "$skill\scripts\setup_qwen_asr_env.py"
& $py "$skill\scripts\check_environment.py"
```

For Chinese videos, you can explicitly specify Qwen3-ASR:

```powershell
& $py "$skill\scripts\extract_bilibili.py" "BVxxxx" --out ".\tmp_bili_extract" --parts "1,10,38" --download-audio --transcribe --asr-backend qwen3-asr
```

### 7. Archive Complete Materials

Organize the temporary extraction directory into a long-term material package. This step should be done by default to facilitate follow-up questions and evidence lookups based on the summary.

```powershell
& $py "$skill\scripts\archive_bili_materials.py" --extract-dir ".\tmp_bili_extract" --archive-dir "D:\knowledge\知识库\Rag技术\原始材料\BVxxxx_视频短标题"
```

The long-term material package includes:

- `articles/图文全文.md`: complete image-text Markdown.
- `articles/图文全文.txt`: complete image-text plain text.
- `images/`: image-text images and image list.
- `indexes/图文全集.md`: merged complete image-text body.
- `indexes/图文全集.jsonl`: split by image-text content blocks, suitable for retrieval and Q&A.
- `indexes/图文证据索引.md`: image-text evidence blocks, suitable for adding citations to summaries.
- `indexes/图文证据索引.jsonl`: image-text evidence blocks, suitable for programmatic retrieval.
- `subtitles/txt/`: complete plain text subtitles for each part.
- `subtitles/srt/`: complete SRT subtitles and timelines for each part.
- `subtitles/json/`: Bilibili raw subtitle JSON.
- `comments/comments_raw.json`: complete raw comment structure.
- `comments/评论全集.md`: complete comment Markdown.
- `indexes/字幕全集.md`: merged complete subtitles, suitable for human reading.
- `indexes/字幕全集.jsonl`: split by subtitle segments, suitable for retrieval and Q&A.
- `indexes/字幕证据索引.md`: time-segment-merged subtitle evidence blocks, suitable for adding citations to summaries.
- `indexes/字幕证据索引.jsonl`: time-segment-merged subtitle evidence blocks, suitable for programmatic retrieval.
- `indexes/评论全集.jsonl`: split by comment/reply, suitable for retrieval and Q&A.
- `indexes/评论证据索引.jsonl`: evidence blocks generated from comments/replies.
- `indexes/证据索引.jsonl`: merged index of image-text/subtitle evidence and comment evidence.
- `metadata/`: content metadata, subtitle list, image-text list, comment list.
- `metadata/note_budget.json`: note budget generated from content information volume and interaction quality, used to control distillation granularity for long/short videos and image-text posts, and to hint at visual supplementation needs when subtitles are sparse.

### 8. Read Budget Before Writing, Verify SNR After Writing

Check the budget before writing notes. The budget is the goal for this note, not a remedial report after writing:

```powershell
Get-Content -Encoding UTF8 "D:\knowledge\知识库\Rag技术\原始材料\BVxxxx_视频短标题\metadata\note_budget.json"
```

First determine the key points:

- Recommended character range: `recommended_note_chars_min` to `recommended_note_chars_max`.
- Writing granularity: `granularity` and `writing_guidance`.
- Information baseline: for videos check `duration_minutes`, `subtitle_chars`; for image-text check `content_chars`, `reading_minutes_estimate`.
- Subtitle density: for videos check `subtitle_chars_per_minute` and `visual_dependency`; when long video subtitles are too few, supplement keyframes/OCR/multimodal visual understanding first.
- Quality multiplier: `quality_multiplier` and `quality_metrics`, used to judge whether retaining more detail is worthwhile.
- Evidence scale: `all_evidence_blocks`, used to decide how much evidence key judgments need to cover.

After writing the final Markdown, score the note using the budget in the archive directory:

```powershell
& $py "$skill\scripts\score_bili_note.py" `
  --archive-dir "D:\knowledge\知识库\Rag技术\原始材料\BVxxxx_视频短标题" `
 --note-path "D:\knowledge\知识库\Rag技术\观点X：视频短标题.md" `
  --out "D:\knowledge\知识库\Rag技术\原始材料\BVxxxx_视频短标题\metadata\note_score.json"
```

You can also write the scoring results directly into the note body:

```powershell
& $py "$skill\scripts\update_note_budget_section.py" `
  --archive-dir "D:\knowledge\知识库\Rag技术\原始材料\BVxxxx_视频短标题" `
 --note-path "D:\knowledge\知识库\Rag技术\观点X：视频短标题.md"
```

Key items to check:

- `status`: `too_short` indicates high omission risk, `too_long` indicates possible redundant padding, `ok` means within the pre-writing recommended range.
- `quality_multiplier`: interaction quality multiplier formed by likes, favorites, coins, comments, danmaku, shares, views, and days since publication.
- `actual_compression_ratio`: note characters / subtitle characters. Long videos should allow higher total characters but still maintain compression.
- `note_chars_per_minute`: how many note characters per minute of video. Long courses should not approach the same total character count as short videos.
- `evidence_reference_ratio`: proportion of cited evidence blocks in the note. Key judgments must be traceable to image-text evidence `O...`, subtitle evidence `Pxx@...`, or comment evidence `C...`; the body uses unified numeric numbering, and end-of-text numbered footnotes and reference-style link definitions must point to archived files containing complete evidence IDs.

## Note Writing Style

Default output must be "learning-oriented notes", not directory dumps, part-by-part logs, or evidence lists. After reading, there should be a sense of "I really learned something".

### Recommended Structure

1. `# Title`
2. `## What You Should Gain After Learning`: use 5-8 items to clearly state what readers can understand, judge, or accomplish after learning.
3. `## One-Sentence Summary`: state the video's most core judgment, avoiding merely restating the title.
4. `## Applicable Scenarios and Prerequisites`: who this content suits and doesn't suit, and what readers need to know first.
5. `## Knowledge Map`: clarify core concepts, modules, processes, and their relationships. Course-type videos need module tables; short opinion videos need argument chains.
6. `## Core Concept Cards`: write each important concept as "what it is, why it matters, how to use it, common misconceptions, related evidence".
7. `## Methods or Processes`: extract operations, architectures, decision flows, parameter choices, and evaluation methods from the original content into reusable steps.
8. `## Key Insights`: write the judgments the creator truly wants to express, distinguishing "factual descriptions, experiential judgments, recommended practices, limiting conditions".
9. `## Practice Checklist`: provide actionable steps, check items, failure signals, and troubleshooting directions.
10. `## Pitfalls and Counterexamples`: organize pitfalls, controversies, misconceptions, and boundary conditions mentioned in the video and comments.
11. `## Self-Test Questions`: write 5-10 questions with brief answers to help humans or Agents check if they've learned.
12. `## Evidence and Source Locations`: only place key evidence citations; don't let evidence drown out learning content.
13. `## Sources, Coverage, and Limitations`: place URL, BVID, UP, publish time, subtitle/comment coverage, raw material paths, and limitations at the end.

### Writing Standards

- Explain "why" and "how to transfer/use" first, then list "what they said".
- For course-type long videos, organize by learning modules, not mechanical compression by part. Each module should include at least: learning objectives, core concepts, key steps, common pitfalls, actionable conclusions.
- For opinion-type short videos, organize as "problem background -> author's judgment -> evidence -> applicable boundaries -> inspiration for users".
- For technical tutorials and long image-text articles, preserve architecture, data flow, code logic, configuration items, image conclusions, evaluation methods, and troubleshooting paths.
- If long video subtitle/transcript density is too low, supplement visual evidence first; without multimodal visual capability, clearly mark the current note as "limited compilation based on subtitles/metadata".
- Only write learning-valuable content from comments: corrections, supplementary cases, practical experience, alternative approaches, controversy points.
- Evidence citations serve learning; don't turn notes into citation lists. The body defaults to unified academic-style numeric numbering like `[1][2]`; image-text evidence, subtitle evidence, and comment evidence share one numbering set, incrementing by first appearance order in the body. Don't stuff long `O<opus_id>-E001`, `Pxx@hh:mm:ss-hh:mm:ss`, or `C<rpid>` directly into body paragraphs.
- Place `## Evidence Footnotes` before `## Sources, Coverage, and Limitations`. Footnotes use ordered lists to state numbers and evidence links, e.g., `1. [Image-text Evidence E006](原始材料/O.../indexes/图文证据索引.md#O...-E006)`; after the list, place reference-style link definitions, e.g., `[1]: 原始材料/O.../indexes/图文证据索引.md#O...-E006 "Image-text Evidence E006"`, so `[1]` in the body is clickable.
- Keep `## Evidence and Source Locations` as an evidence overview, but only write numbers like `[1]`, `[2]` in the overview, no longer displaying long evidence IDs directly.
- Set targets according to `note_budget.json` before writing, then start writing the note; post-writing scoring is only for verification and fine-tuning—don't defer major length decisions to the scoring stage.
- When the budget is short or post-writing score is too short, prioritize adding "concept explanations, flowchart-style text, practice checklists, self-test questions, counterexamples and boundaries" rather than just adding summary paragraphs.
- Popularity is an auxiliary signal for "worth writing more", not a substitute for evidence. Likes, favorites, comments, danmaku, coins, shares, and days since publication will raise or lower recommended character counts, but expansion must come from image-text body, subtitles, comment evidence, and content structure.

### Failure Signals

- Large blocks of source info at the beginning, leaving readers unsure what they've learned after reading for a while.
- Only "core viewpoints/part distillations/representative evidence" without concept explanations, method steps, and self-tests.
- Compressing each part into one sentence, leaving readers of long courses still unsure how to proceed.
- Very few subtitles in long videos without noting visual dependency or supplementing keyframes/OCR/visual understanding.
- Only summarizing the author's stance without writing applicable conditions, counterexamples, and failure scenarios.
- Comments section merely listing hot comments without converting them into corrections, supplements, or practical reminders.

Don't write "only looked at title/directory" content as "complete extraction". If only partial subtitles were fetched or only some parts transcribed, clearly list the coverage.

## Bilibili Subtitle Notes

- Normal `/x/player/v2` may only return `ai-zh` subtitle metadata with empty `subtitle_url`.
- The web player API `/x/player/wbi/v2` often returns actual AI subtitle URLs.
- AI subtitles often misrecognize technical terms: RAG may become RG, ROG, rap; LangChain may become non chain, long chain; reranker may become "瑞 rank".
- Correct terminology during summarization by combining part titles and technical context.

## Bilibili Image-Text Notes

- Image-text/post body should preferably be read from `window.__INITIAL_STATE__` within the page; public polymer post APIs may return risk-control errors.
- Image-text body preserves titles, paragraphs, heading levels, lists, code blocks, link cards, image URLs, and image lists.
- Image-text comment targets are usually not the opus id itself, but `basic.comment_type` and `basic.comment_id_str` in page data; don't force-fit video `type=1/oid=aid` when fetching comments.
- If the user asks you to summarize image meanings in image-text posts, first check `images/` or `images_manifest.json`; when image URLs alone are insufficient to judge content, state that visual content of images was not fully understood.

## Related Files

- `scripts/check_environment.py`: checks whether core flows, web AI subtitles, audio transcription, and test dependencies are available.
- `scripts/setup_qwen_asr_env.py`: creates/updates the shared Qwen3-ASR Python environment.
- `scripts/run_qwen_asr.py`: calls Qwen3-ASR-0.6B, can segment by chunk to avoid VRAM overflow.
- `scripts/run_bili_note.py`: one-click run for video/image-text extraction, comments, archiving, and evidence indexing flows.
- `scripts/extract_bilibili.py`: metadata, subtitle probing, normal subtitles, audio, audio transcription, comment fetching.
- `scripts/extract_bilibili_opus.py`: Bilibili image-text/post body, images, code blocks, and image-text comment fetching.
- `scripts/fetch_browser_ai_subtitles.py`: downloads Bilibili AI subtitles via logged-in web player.
- `scripts/archive_bili_materials.py`: archives complete materials, generates full-text indexes, evidence indexes, and note budgets with subtitle density/visual dependency hints.
- `scripts/score_bili_note.py`: verifies final note length, compression ratio, evidence citations, and visual dependency hints according to `metadata/note_budget.json`.
- `scripts/update_note_budget_section.py`: writes budget, interaction quality, and SNR scores back into the Markdown note.
- `references/bilibili-api-notes.md`: API details and known pitfalls.

- If the currently connected model or tool cannot view images, you must tell the user: keyframe understanding is an advanced visual capability requiring multimodal models, OCR tools, or manual review; currently only limited notes based on subtitles/metadata can be generated with coverage noted.
- The final note and user reply should relay `visual_dependency.warnings` and state whether visual evidence has been supplemented.

## Dependencies and Environment Check

The default route aims for zero third-party Python dependencies: video metadata, public subtitles, image-text body, image lists, comments, archiving, evidence indexes, and note budgets are all done with the standard library. Web AI subtitles and audio transcription are enhancement routes, not startup requirements.

On first use, machine change, suspected missing dependencies, or before using web AI subtitles / audio transcription fallback, run first:

```powershell
$skill = "$env:USERPROFILE\.codex\skills\bili-note"
$py = "python"
& $py "$skill\scripts\check_environment.py"
```

Choose the route based on the results:

- `public_subtitles_comments_archive=OK`: prefer the default subtitle/image-text, comment, and archiving flow.
- `browser_ai_subtitles=OK`: when the public API only returns `ai-zh` and `subtitle_url` is empty, use Chrome + `web-access` web AI subtitles.
- `audio_asr_fallback=OK`: only use audio transcription when both subtitles and web AI subtitles are unavailable and the user truly needs a full transcript. Prefer shared Qwen3-ASR for Chinese or unspecified languages; prefer Whisper-family backends for explicitly foreign-language videos.
- When an enhancement capability is missing, only state that route is temporarily unavailable; do not claim the entire skill is unusable.
- Web login state is only used via `web-access` authorized Chrome pages; do not read or copy cookies/profiles, and do not force-kill the user's browser process. Without Chrome + `web-access`, skip web AI subtitles and explain the coverage.

## Default Flow

1. Clarify what the user wants: video or image-text link, whether comments are needed, save path, whether full materials or just distilled content are required.
2. If it's the first use, dependency status is unclear, subtitle fetching failed, or the user requests audio transcription, use `check_environment.py` first to determine available routes.
3. Prefer `run_bili_note.py` to one-click complete automatable parts. It automatically recognizes `/video/BV...`, `/opus/...`, `/dynamic/...`, or plain opus ids.
4. For image-text/posts, use the `extract_bilibili_opus.py` route: fetch body, title, author, publish time, images, code blocks, and image-text evidence index; fetch image-text comments when the user adds `--comments`.
5. For videos, prefer downloading subtitles:
   - When normal subtitle URLs are available, use `--download-subtitles` directly.
   - If the normal API shows `ai-zh` but `subtitle_url` is empty, do not say "no subtitles"; switch to the "web AI subtitles" flow.
   - If subtitles are still unavailable, download audio as needed and transcribe with local automatic speech recognition. Prefer Qwen3-ASR for Chinese, and Whisper-family backends for explicitly foreign languages.
6. When the user requests comments, use `--comments` to fetch top-level and child comments; filter out check-ins, resource requests, ads, chitchat, and other non-technical content when writing the note.
7. Archive raw materials: store complete subtitles or image-text body, images, full comments, metadata, and JSONL indexes in a long-term directory next to the knowledge base.
8. Set targets before writing: you must read `metadata/note_budget.json` first, using the recommended character range, compression ratio target, writing granularity, interaction quality multiplier, evidence block count, and `visual_dependency` as writing goals for this note. Videos are benchmarked by duration, subtitle characters, evidence blocks, comment volume, and interaction quality; image-text posts by body length, images/code/evidence blocks, comment volume, and interaction quality.
   - If `visual_dependency.risk` is `medium` or `high`, supplement keyframes/OCR/multimodal visual understanding first, or clearly tell the user that visual understanding capability is currently lacking and a complete analysis cannot be written.
9. Write Markdown according to budget: default to "learning-oriented notes", aiming for humans or Agents to gain concepts, methods, judgment criteria, practical steps, and self-test questions as if finishing a lesson or tutorial; decide detail level by budget, and do not write long courses and short videos with similar word counts. Place sources, coverage, and archive paths in the latter part. Body evidence defaults to academic-style numbering like `[1][2]`, without directly piling long evidence IDs.
10. Verify after writing: use `score_bili_note.py` to validate note character count, compression ratio, per-minute/per-article density, and evidence citation ratio. Scoring is only for QA and fine-tuning, not a substitute for pre-writing targets; when too short, prioritize adding "learning takeaways, knowledge maps, concept cards, practical workflows, pitfalls, self-test questions" rather than just stacking part summaries or paragraph summaries.

- Recommended character range: `recommended_note_chars_min` to `recommended_note_chars_max`.
- Writing granularity: `granularity` and `writing_guidance`.

- Subtitle density: for videos check `subtitle_chars_per_minute` and `visual_dependency`; when long video subtitles are too few, supplement keyframes/OCR/multimodal visual understanding first.
- Quality multiplier: `quality_multiplier` and `quality_metrics`, used to judge whether retaining more detail is worthwhile.
- Evidence scale: `all_evidence_blocks`, used to decide how much evidence key judgments need to cover.

```powershell

  --archive-dir "D:\knowledge\知识库\Rag技术\原始材料\BVxxxx_视频短标题" `
```

Key items to check:

- `status`: `too_short` indicates high omission risk, `too_long` indicates possible redundant padding, `ok` means within the pre-writing recommended range.
- `quality_multiplier`: interaction quality multiplier formed by likes, favorites, coins, comments, danmaku, shares, views, and days since publication.
- `actual_compression_ratio`: note characters / subtitle characters. Long videos should allow higher total characters but still maintain compression.
- `note_chars_per_minute`: how many note characters per minute of video. Long courses should not approach the same total character count as short videos.
- `evidence_reference_ratio`: proportion of cited evidence blocks in the note. Key judgments must be traceable to image-text evidence `O...`, subtitle evidence `Pxx@...`, or comment evidence `C...`; the body uses unified numeric numbering, and end-of-text numbered footnotes and reference-style link definitions must point to archived files containing complete evidence IDs.

## Note Writing Style

Default output must be "learning-oriented notes", not directory dumps, part-by-part logs, or evidence lists. After reading, there should be a sense of "I really learned something".

### Recommended Structure

1. `# Title`
2. `## What You Should Gain After Learning`: use 5-8 items to clearly state what readers can understand, judge, or accomplish after learning.
3. `## One-Sentence Summary`: state the video's most core judgment, avoiding merely restating the title.
4. `## Applicable Scenarios and Prerequisites`: who this content suits and doesn't suit, and what readers need to know first.
5. `## Knowledge Map`: clarify core concepts, modules, processes, and their relationships. Course-type videos need module tables; short opinion videos need argument chains.
6. `## Core Concept Cards`: write each important concept as "what it is, why it matters, how to use it, common misconceptions, related evidence".
7. `## Methods or Processes`: extract operations, architectures, decision flows, parameter choices, and evaluation methods from the original content into reusable steps.
8. `## Key Insights`: write the judgments the creator truly wants to express, distinguishing "factual descriptions, experiential judgments, recommended practices, limiting conditions".
9. `## Practice Checklist`: provide actionable steps, check items, failure signals, and troubleshooting directions.
10. `## Pitfalls and Counterexamples`: organize pitfalls, controversies, misconceptions, and boundary conditions mentioned in the video and comments.
11. `## Self-Test Questions`: write 5-10 questions with brief answers to help humans or Agents check if they've learned.
12. `## Evidence and Source Locations`: only place key evidence citations; don't let evidence drown out learning content.
13. `## Sources, Coverage, and Limitations`: place URL, BVID, UP, publish time, subtitle/comment coverage, raw material paths, and limitations at the end.

### Writing Standards

- Explain "why" and "how to transfer/use" first, then list "what they said".
- For course-type long videos, organize by learning modules, not mechanical compression by part. Each module should include at least: learning objectives, core concepts, key steps, common pitfalls, actionable conclusions.
- For opinion-type short videos, organize as "problem background -> author's judgment -> evidence -> applicable boundaries -> inspiration for users".
- For technical tutorials and long image-text articles, preserve architecture, data flow, code logic, configuration items, image conclusions, evaluation methods, and troubleshooting paths.
- If long video subtitle/transcript density is too low, supplement visual evidence first; without multimodal visual capability, clearly mark the current note as "limited compilation based on subtitles/metadata".
- Only write learning-valuable content from comments: corrections, supplementary cases, practical experience, alternative approaches, controversy points.
- Evidence citations serve learning; don't turn notes into citation lists. The body defaults to unified academic-style numeric numbering like `[1][2]`; image-text evidence, subtitle evidence, and comment evidence share one numbering set, incrementing by first appearance order in the body. Don't stuff long `O<opus_id>-E001`, `Pxx@hh:mm:ss-hh:mm:ss`, or `C<rpid>` directly into body paragraphs.
- Place `## Evidence Footnotes` before `## Sources, Coverage, and Limitations`. Footnotes use ordered lists to state numbers and evidence links, e.g., `1. [Image-text Evidence E006](原始材料/O.../indexes/图文证据索引.md#O...-E006)`; after the list, place reference-style link definitions, e.g., `[1]: 原始材料/O.../indexes/图文证据索引.md#O...-E006 "Image-text Evidence E006"`, so `[1]` in the body is clickable.
- Keep `## Evidence and Source Locations` as an evidence overview, but only write numbers like `[1]`, `[2]` in the overview, no longer displaying long evidence IDs directly.
- Set targets according to `note_budget.json` before writing, then start writing the note; post-writing scoring is only for verification and fine-tuning—don't defer major length decisions to the scoring stage.
- When the budget is short or post-writing score is too short, prioritize adding "concept explanations, flowchart-style text, practice checklists, self-test questions, counterexamples and boundaries" rather than just adding summary paragraphs.
- Popularity is an auxiliary signal for "worth writing more", not a substitute for evidence. Likes, favorites, comments, danmaku, coins, shares, and days since publication will raise or lower recommended character counts, but expansion must come from image-text body, subtitles, comment evidence, and content structure.

### Failure Signals

- Large blocks of source info at the beginning, leaving readers unsure what they've learned after reading for a while.
- Only "core viewpoints/part distillations/representative evidence" without concept explanations, method steps, and self-tests.
- Compressing each part into one sentence, leaving readers of long courses still unsure how to proceed.
- Very few subtitles in long videos without noting visual dependency or supplementing keyframes/OCR/visual understanding.
- Only summarizing the author's stance without writing applicable conditions, counterexamples, and failure scenarios.
- Comments section merely listing hot comments without converting them into corrections, supplements, or practical reminders.

Don't write "only looked at title/directory" content as "complete extraction". If only partial subtitles were fetched or only some parts transcribed, clearly list the coverage.

## Bilibili Subtitle Notes

- Normal `/x/player/v2` may only return `ai-zh` subtitle metadata with empty `subtitle_url`.
- The web player API `/x/player/wbi/v2` often returns actual AI subtitle URLs.
- AI subtitles often misrecognize technical terms: RAG may become RG, ROG, rap; LangChain may become non chain, long chain; reranker may become "瑞 rank".
- Correct terminology during summarization by combining part titles and technical context.

## Bilibili Image-Text Notes

- Image-text/post body should preferably be read from `window.__INITIAL_STATE__` within the page; public polymer post APIs may return risk-control errors.
- Image-text body preserves titles, paragraphs, heading levels, lists, code blocks, link cards, image URLs, and image lists.
- Image-text comment targets are usually not the opus id itself, but `basic.comment_type` and `basic.comment_id_str` in page data; don't force-fit video `type=1/oid=aid` when fetching comments.
- If the user asks you to summarize image meanings in image-text posts, first check `images/` or `images_manifest.json`; when image URLs alone are insufficient to judge content, state that visual content of images was not fully understood.

- `scripts/check_environment.py`: checks whether core flows, web AI subtitles, audio transcription, and test dependencies are available.
- `scripts/setup_qwen_asr_env.py`: creates/updates the shared Qwen3-ASR Python environment.

# Bili Note

把 B站视频和图文动态变成可检索、可复用的 Markdown 知识笔记。视频优先拿字幕；字幕拿不到时再转写音频；图文优先抓正文、图片和代码块；用户要评论区时抓取评论并过滤无关讨论。

联网或登录态操作必须先使用 `web-access`。

网页 AI 字幕当前只支持 Chrome + `web-access` 路线：让已登录的 B站页面自己请求字幕接口。不要把 Edge、Playwright 临时浏览器或原生 CDP 端口当成等价替代，除非脚本已经明确支持。

Bili Note 与 DyNote 共享可复用本地资源。默认共享目录是 `%USERPROFILE%\.cache\rimagination-notes`，Qwen3-ASR 环境默认是 `%USERPROFILE%\.cache\rimagination-notes\qwen3-asr-venv`。如果任一 skill 已经安装过 Qwen3-ASR，另一个 skill 必须优先复用，不要重复安装。Hugging Face、Whisper 和 faster-whisper 缓存按本机通用缓存复用。

## 字幕密度与视觉理解

B 站视频优先拿字幕，但字幕/转写不等于完整理解。长视频如果字幕字数明显偏少，可能说明核心信息在画面、PPT、板书、代码演示、屏幕操作或无解说片段中。

- 归档后必须读取 `metadata/note_budget.json`。如果 `visual_dependency.needs_visual_review=true`，不要把稀疏字幕写成完整学习笔记。
- 这种情况下，先采用更合适的技术：抽取代表性关键帧或截图，再做 OCR 或多模态视觉理解；必要时重新抓网页 AI 字幕或补本地自动语音识别。
- 如果当前接入的模型或工具不能看图，必须告诉用户：关键帧理解属于高级视觉能力，需要多模态模型、OCR 工具或人工查看；当前只能基于字幕/元数据生成有限笔记并标注覆盖范围。
- 最终笔记和用户回复要转述 `visual_dependency.warnings`，并说明是否已经补了视觉证据。

## 依赖与环境检查

默认路线尽量零第三方 Python 依赖：视频元数据、公开字幕、图文正文、图片清单、评论、归档、证据索引和笔记预算都用标准库完成。网页 AI 字幕和音频转写是增强路线，不是启动门槛。

第一次使用、换机器、用户怀疑依赖不全，或准备使用网页 AI 字幕 / 音频转写兜底时，先运行：

```powershell
$skill = "$env:USERPROFILE\.codex\skills\bili-note"
$py = "python"
& $py "$skill\scripts\check_environment.py"
```

根据检查结果选择路线：

- `public_subtitles_comments_archive=OK`：优先走默认字幕/图文、评论和归档流程。
- `browser_ai_subtitles=OK`：当公开接口只有 `ai-zh` 且 `subtitle_url` 为空时，走 Chrome + `web-access` 网页 AI 字幕。

## 默认流程

1. 读清用户要什么：视频或图文链接、是否要评论区、保存路径、是否需要全文材料或只要提炼。
2. 如果是首次使用、依赖状态不明、字幕抓取失败或用户要求音频转写，先用 `check_environment.py` 判断当前可走路线。
3. 优先用 `run_bili_note.py` 一键完成可自动化部分。它会自动识别 `/video/BV...`、`/opus/...`、`/dynamic/...` 或纯 opus id。
4. 如果是图文/动态，走 `extract_bilibili_opus.py` 路线：抓正文、标题、作者、发布时间、图片、代码块、图文证据索引；用户加 `--comments` 时抓图文评论。
5. 如果是视频，优先下载字幕：
   - 普通字幕 URL 可用时，直接用 `--download-subtitles`。
   - 如果普通接口显示 `ai-zh` 但 `subtitle_url` 为空，不要说“没有字幕”；改走“网页 AI 字幕”流程。
   - 如果字幕仍不可得，再按需要下载音频并用本地自动语音识别转写。中文优先 Qwen3-ASR，明确外语优先 Whisper 系后端。
6. 用户要求评论区时，用 `--comments` 抓取主评论和子评论；写入笔记时过滤打卡、求资料、广告、闲聊等技术无关内容。
7. 归档原始材料：把完整字幕或图文正文、图片、完整评论、元数据和 JSONL 索引存到知识库旁边的长期目录。
8. 写前定标：必须先读取 `metadata/note_budget.json`，把推荐字数区间、压缩比目标、写作粒度、互动质量倍率、证据块数量和 `visual_dependency` 作为本次笔记的写作目标。视频按时长、字幕字数、证据块、评论量和互动质量定标；图文按正文长度、图片/代码/证据块、评论量和互动质量定标。
   - 如果 `visual_dependency.risk` 是 `medium` 或 `high`，先补关键帧/OCR/多模态视觉理解，或明确告诉用户当前缺少视觉理解能力，不能写成完整解析。
9. 按预算写 Markdown：默认写成“学习型笔记”，目标是让人或 Agent 像学完一节课或读完一篇教程一样获得概念、方法、判断标准、实践步骤和自测题；根据预算决定详略，不要把长课和短视频写成差不多字数。来源、覆盖范围和归档路径放到后半部分。正文证据默认用论文式编号 `[1][2]`，不直接堆长证据 ID。
10. 写后验收：用 `score_bili_note.py` 校验笔记字数、压缩比、每分钟/每篇笔记密度和证据引用比例。评分只做 QA 和微调，不代替写前定标；太短时优先补“学习收获、知识地图、概念卡、实战流程、坑点、自测题”，不要只堆分P摘要或段落摘要。

## 笔记写法

默认输出必须是“学习型笔记”，不是目录搬运、分P流水账或证据清单。读完后应有“我真的学会了一些东西”的获得感。

### 推荐结构

1. `# 标题`
2. `## 学完你应该获得什么`：用 5-8 条写清楚读者学完后能理解、判断或完成什么。
3. `## 一句话总论`：说明视频最核心的判断，避免只复述标题。
4. `## 适用场景与前置知识`：这套内容适合谁、不适合谁，读者需要先知道什么。
5. `## 知识地图`：把核心概念、模块、流程和它们之间的关系讲清楚。课程型视频要有模块表；短观点视频要有论证链。
6. `## 核心概念卡`：每个重要概念都写成“是什么、为什么重要、怎么用、常见误区、相关证据”。
7. `## 方法或流程`：把原内容中的操作、架构、决策流程、参数选择、评估方法抽成可复用步骤。
8. `## 关键洞察`：写作者真正想表达的判断，区分“事实描述、经验判断、推荐做法、限制条件”。
9. `## 实践清单`：给出可以照着做的步骤、检查项、失败信号和排错方向。
10. `## 坑点与反例`：整理视频和评论区提到的踩坑、争议、误区、边界条件。
11. `##自测题`：写 5-10 个问题和简短答案，帮助人或 Agent 检查是否学会。
12. `## 证据与原文位置`：只放关键证据引用，不要让证据淹没学习内容。
13. `## 来源、覆盖与局限`：URL、BVID、UP、发布时间、字幕/评论覆盖、原始材料路径和局限放在后面。

### 写作标准

- 先解释“为什么”和“怎么迁移使用”，再列“他说了什么”。
- 对课程型长视频，按学习模块组织，不要按分P机械压缩。每个模块至少包含：学习目标、核心概念、关键步骤、常见坑、可操作结论。
- 对观点型短视频，按“问题背景 -> 作者判断 -> 论据 -> 适用边界 -> 对用户的启发”组织。
- 对技术教程和图文长文，保留架构、数据流、代码思路、配置项、图片结论、评估方式和排错路径。
- 如果长视频字幕/转写密度过低，先补视觉证据；没有多模态视觉能力时，明确把当前笔记标为“基于字幕/元数据的有限整理”。
- 评论区只写有学习价值的内容：纠错、补充案例、实践经验、替代方案、争议点。
- 证据引用服务于学习，不要把笔记写成引用列表。正文默认使用统一的论文式数字编号，例如 `[1][2]`；图文证据、字幕证据、评论证据共用一套编号，按正文首次出现顺序递增。不要在正文段落里直接塞很长的 `O<opus_id>-E001`、`Pxx@hh:mm:ss-hh:mm:ss` 或 `C<rpid>`。
- 在 `## 来源、覆盖与局限` 之前放 `## 证据脚注`。脚注用有序列表写明编号和证据链接，例如 `1. [图文证据 E006](原始材料/O.../indexes/图文证据索引.md#O...-E006)`；列表后再放 reference-style 链接定义，例如 `[1]: 原始材料/O.../indexes/图文证据索引.md#O...-E006 "图文证据 E006"`，让正文里的 `[1]` 也能点击跳转。
- 保留 `## 证据与原文位置` 作为证据总览，但总览里也只写 `[1]`、`[2]` 这样的编号，不再直接显示长证据 ID。
- 写前先按 `note_budget.json` 定标，再开始写笔记；写后评分只用于验收和微调，不要把主要长度决策推迟到评分阶段。
- 预算偏短或写后评分过短时，优先补“概念解释、流程图式文字、实践清单、自测题、反例和边界”，不要只增加摘要段落。
- 热度是“值得多写”的辅助信号，不是替代证据。点赞、收藏、评论、弹幕、投币、分享和发布距今天数会提高或降低推荐字数，但扩写必须来自图文正文、字幕、评论证据和内容结构。

### 不合格信号

- 开头大段来源信息，读者看半天还不知道学到了什么。
- 只有“核心观点/分P提炼/代表性证据”，没有概念解释、方法步骤和自测。
- 把每个分P压成一句话，长课程读完仍不知道怎么做。
- 长视频字幕极少，却没有提示画面依赖，也没有补关键帧/OCR/视觉理解。
- 只总结作者立场，不写适用条件、反例和失败场景。
- 评论区只是罗列热评，没有转化成纠错、补充或实践提醒。

不要把“只看了标题/目录”的内容写成“完整提取”。如果只抓到部分字幕或只转写了部分分P，明确列出覆盖范围。

## B站字幕注意事项

- 普通 `/x/player/v2` 可能只返回 `ai-zh` 字幕元信息，`subtitle_url` 为空。
- 网页播放器接口 `/x/player/wbi/v2` 常能返回真正的 AI 字幕 URL。
- AI 字幕常把技术词识别错：RAG 可能识别成 RG、ROG、rap；LangChain 可能识别成 non chain、long chain；reranker 可能识别成“瑞 rank”。
- 总结时要结合分P标题和技术语境校正术语。

## B站图文注意事项

- 图文/动态正文优先从页面内的 `window.__INITIAL_STATE__`读取；公开 polymer 动态接口可能返回风控错误。
- 图文正文会保留标题、段落、标题层级、列表、代码块、链接卡片、图片 URL 和图片清单。
- 图文评论对象通常不是 opus id 本身，而是页面数据里的 `basic.comment_type` 和 `basic.comment_id_str`；抓评论时不要硬套视频的 `type=1/oid=aid`。
- 如果用户让你总结图文中的图片含义，先检查 `images/` 或 `images_manifest.json`；仅凭图片 URL 不足以判断内容时，应说明图片视觉内容未被完整理解。
